1.init: comment cadence_filter - remove a recording rhythm
1.name: comment

2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
cadence_filter removes a rhythm that the recording put into the data, not the movement.

WHAT CADENCE IS:
A sensor running at one rate and delivered at another leaves a pattern in the data that repeats every few frames. Shadow files recorded at 100 Hz and saved at 60 are an example: from one saved frame to the next, the movement advances by two sensor frames, then two, then one, over and over - a cycle three frames long. A sensor running at about 33 Hz and upsampled to 100 Hz leaves the same kind of three-frame cycle.

That pattern is not movement, but every measure built on frame-to-frame change reads it as movement, at a fixed frequency, all the time. It inflates jerk, it triggers glitch detectors, and it is the reason a still performer can look busy.

HOW IT REMOVES IT:
Each number that arrives is averaged with the ones before it - a causal moving average over 'window' frames. A pattern that repeats every N frames averages to nothing over a window of N frames, so the default window of 3 removes a three-frame cadence exactly.

Causal means it uses only past frames, so it works on a live stream. The price is a fixed lag: half a window less half a frame, which is one frame at a window of 3.

WHAT IT AVERAGES:
Every number on its own, with no knowledge of what the numbers are. That is right for positions, and close enough for rotations that change little from frame to frame. It is not right across a jump in representation: a quaternion that flips sign, or an axis-angle that wraps round, inside the window blends two descriptions of the same rotation into a wrong one for a frame or two. The quaternions it produces are not renormalized.

SYNTAX:
cadence_filter

EXAMPLE:
cadence_filter

INPUTS:

pose in:
Any array of numbers - a pose, a list, a single value. Each arrival is filtered and sent from 'pose out'.

trans in:
The same, kept separately, sent from 'trans out'. The two inlets have their own histories, so they can run on different streams.

PROPERTIES:

enable:
Off, or a window below 2, passes the data through unchanged.

window:
How many frames are averaged. Set it to the length of the cadence cycle.

OUTPUTS:

pose out / trans out:
The filtered data, the same shape as it came in. A single number goes out as a single number.

The history starts out filled with the first frame, so there is no ramp up from zero. Changing the window, or the size of what arrives, starts it again.

A WORD ON TRANSLATION:
The translation channel comes from a body-mounted sensor that projects from the body and has mass, so it flops in vigorous movement - especially vertical movement - in ways the joint rotations do not. It wants its own, heavier filtering after this, and it should never be gate-opened on the assumption that a large change means real motion.

RELATED:
check_burst flags frames where the data jumps implausibly. quaternion_diff_and_axis measures how much each joint turns per frame - the measure the cadence shows up in.
